cells.remarks: Registers gift of 4½ vēlī and odd of land called Tillaimēnippākkam, in the same village, inambalāp-stānam made by Muppuchchundali, an adukkalai-pāṇḍu-penḍu (maid-servant of the royal household) for the maintenance of persons supplying flowers to the god and goddess and for sounding a bell every day by the street, leading to Ediriliśōlan-tiruttōppu. This gift was ratified, at the request of the donatrix, by a royal order signed by the Secretary Rājēndraśōla-mūvēndavēļān. The name of the garden is shown originally granted (tax-free) in the 7th year of the king to a certain Gautamān Sivakumaran Arulāla-bhaṭṭan alias Savarapackaravarti of Uttamasōla-maṅgalam in Rājādhirāja-vaļanādu, from whose sons purchase was made subsequently.

cells.place: Several stones built into the walls of Aguḷīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Stones lost and misplaced. Begins with the introduction of the king and records that the entire village instituted under orders of the king by the officer Rājēndraśōḷa-Mūvēndavēḷān in the 29th year of his reign, regarding the title of some temple lands which had been originally given in the 4th year of Uttama-Chōḷa and which were not in the enjoyment of the temple for thirty-five years. States that the assembly (sabhā), of the village against whom the decision was given, agreed to make this free of taxes to the temple in lieu of 400 kāśu which the king ordered paid against the 200 which had been originally received by them (probably as tax-money).

cells.remarks: Registers an order of Gāṅgēyan to the merchants of Marudanguḍi, Niyanam and Aḷakāpuri fixing the kaḍamai and oḍu (or achchuvari) to be levied on certain lands in Aḷakāpuri newly purchased as purru, at the rate of one-half of the yield. It also states that the getters the fixing by Kaṇḍan Uḍaiyāñjēyāṉ alias Gāṅgēyaṉ of the kaḍamai and kuḍimai taxes on Kunravayal at Tiruviṅgaikkudi, which had been previously collected according to the Gāṅgēyaṉ-amāṇi to the god Dēśivināyaka-Piḷḷaiyār in the temple of Tiruviṅgaikkudi-Mahādēva, at the rates prevailing in Aḷakāyūr-nāḍu, and the other taxes like achchuvari at the standard of the rate prevailing on the purru lands at Tiruviṅgaikkudi.

cells.location: Tirupputtūr
cells.place: South wall of the central shrine in the Tiruttaḷīśvara temple.
cells.king: Jaṭāvarman alias Tribhuvanachakravartin Pāṇḍyadēva ‘who was pleased to take all countries’
cells.remarks: Registers that Śiruppaṇai-Nāyaka who was ruling over Piṅgāymalai-śīrmai as his nāyakkattanam, confirmed the grant of lands in several villages in Piṅguṇra-nāḍu which had already been endowed, and remitted the taxes due from them in favour of the temple of Tiruttaḷīyāṇḍa-Nāyaṉār at Tirupputtūr, for offerings, in Kēraḷaśiṅga-vaḷanāḍu, for offerings and worship to the deity and for the conduct of the morning service called Siruppaṇaiyākaṉ-śandi newly instituted by himself. Damaged and beginning lost. Seems to refer to the settlement by the Aḍaivāśikkār of Tirupputtūr-śīrmai of a dispute between two communities regarding the temple-lands in some villages in view of the parties, viz., the Ambalakkudi of Virūyāchachilai.

cells.location: Dēvarāyapuram
cells.place: Slab set up against the front wall of the Āñjanēya shrine.
cells.date: Śaka 1469, Plavaṅga, Śrāvaṇa, ba. 30, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 267: Śaka 1469, Plavaṅga, Śravaṇa, ba. 30, Monday = A.D. 1547, August 15, Monday ; 36.]
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of Dēvarāyapura-agrahāram to the learned men of that village by China-Avubhalayya-dēva-Mahārāja, son of Narasingarāja of the lunar race and the Ātrēya gōtra, for the merit of Narasingarāja Raghupatirāja Avubhalarāja. The village granted is stated to be situated in Siruvōla-sīma which was given to the donor as amaramagani, the king's order being made in the presence of the god Paṇḍaraṅgi Viṭṭhalēśvara. Damaged. Seems to refer to the setting up of the image of Hanumān in the temple. Mentions Chintakuṇṭa.

cells.remarks: States that Kappara Mallanaimma of Dāmajjala gave a cow, etc., had an iron-drum made and gave to the temple of Bhōgānāthadēva and erected a shed for keeping the drum. Dāmajjala is stated to be situated in Oḍayala-sthala, a territory of Vidyāmu Kommarāju. In another slab in the same place, and damaged inscription dated in Śaka 1235 which mentions a certain Mahārāja (name lost) and his gifts. Records the obeisance of the stone-cutter (kāśa) Sāra- [t]i-jana to the god Chennakēśavasvāmin of Dāma-gjala.

Refers to Muddi-kēra-sthala and the 56 countries.

cells.place: Slab set up in front of the Sāluva temple.
cells.remarks: Registers gifts of lands to the temple of Chennakēśavasvāmi (also called Chennarāya) made by Kāmarasavva-Ayyagāru for the daily worship of the god. The gifts are stated to have been made in the presence of god Viṭhaladēva, on the bank of the Tuṅgabhadrā and on the occasion of Utthāna-dvādaśi, for the merit of the king and Narasasiṁharāya-Voḍayalu. Pālagīri is said to be situated in Sāluva-sthala. Registers also gifts of land made by Rāchīrāja Eram-Timmaiya to the same temple for the merit of the Rāya and Narasā-Nāyaka.

cells.remarks: Records a gift of land at Kaḷakere made by Bamma-Gāvuḍa and the Gāvuḍas of the village of Bāḷambīḍ to one who died fighting in a raid made by Kaḷḷadēva-Daṇḍa-nāyaka the Sunkaḍādhikāri (tax-officer) of Hanuṅgal-500 district, to Vimalaśaktidēva for the benefit of the temple of Brahmēśvaradēva attached to the temple of Rāmēśvara. The raid was made by the army of the king, Siddhuḍi-Daṇḍanāyaka, Harihara-Gāvuḍa, Heggaḍe Bīraṇa and Sixty Families (okkal). Also records some minor gifts to the same temple.

cells.date:
Śaka 1280, Kīlaka, Vaiśākha, ba. 30, Monday, solar eclipse, Monday, saṅkrāmaṇa, Vyatīpāta. [date-calculation appendix, No. 130: VIJAYANAGARA.
Vīra-Bukkarāya.
Śaka 1290, Kilaka, Vaisākha, ba. 30, Monday, solar eclipse, saṅkrānti, Vyatīpāta.
Irregular. In the given year, Vaisākha amāvāsya fell on A.D. 1368, May 17,
Wednesday (not Monday). There was nei her solar eclipse nor saṅkrānti on this
day, as quoted in the re ord. But in the next year, Saumya, there was a solar
eclipse on Jyēshtha, ba. 30. corresponding to Monday, at 14 and lasted till
11 of Tuesday, 5th June A.D. 1369, when there occurred a solar eclipse. In this
case the month quoted in the record would be a cording to the Pūrṇimānta
system. The saṅkrānti had, however, occurred in the previous month, on Satur-
day, 26th May.]
cells.remarks: States that (this is) the service (prayer) of Saḍāśivādē-jēndra of Sōde. Mentions Kaṇakāvati.

cells.remarks: In modern characters. Purports to record that samaya-mudali-kayakkolapattagam and uḥhaya-samayappattagam-pattagam made some social and other privileges made by Virappa-Nāyaka and executed by the committee of the fire (arsan) communities residing at Madurai to certain types of pullivēṇḍan, a member of the Idangai community of Varudanpatti, in recognition of his having worked to fight Orukkāppudaiyāyan, the head of the Valangai community who was a source of great trouble to them.

cells.place: Another slab lying in the place of Rāmaliṅga †
cells.remarks: States that at the request of a certain Mariyappa, certain lands in the villages of Kere-grāma and Khaidōtti-grāma in Gājanūru-sīme, made by the king to the teacher Chamarūrti Rāchavaṇīyadēva, the dis-ciple of Chamarārti-Svāmimaṭha Karti-Basavarajadeva sometime previously, was now confirmed by a deed. Gives the ancestry of the chief for three generations. Mentioned therein are the mahā-madans Burāna-Khān, Sābhā-Khān Lādā-Khān and Abū-Khān, from whom the lands in question were purchased.

cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction ‘Pugalāndu puṇari’ etc. States that as the temple of Mummuḍichōḷa-Viṇṇagarālvār at Rājamahēndra-chaturvēdimangalam, a brahmadēya in Kāṇāra-nāḍu a subdivision of Nittavinōda-vaḷanāḍu, was falling to decay, the king’s officers, with a view to the glory of its treasury, during the conflict between the king’s and Loft hand class in the 2nd year of the king’s reign, the assembly of Rājamahēndra-chaturvēdimangalam received a lump sum of 2,000 paṇam and exempted certain lands belonging to it from payment of taxes.

cells.location: FRENCH INDIA. Pondicherry — Puducherry
cells.place: A fourth stone in Jumma Masjid †
cells.remarks: In characters of the 19th century A.D. Records the circumstances of the construction of the tank Āyikuḷam at Muṭṭirā-pāḷaiyam by one Rāya-gūru-Ayyar with the permission of Kṛishṇadēvarāya of Rāyur, who was ruling in the southern country with the minister Appāji. The third Nappōliyōn (Napoleon III) is stated to have given this site for the construction of a fountain in her memory. A Latin version of this record is given on another slab set up in the same place.

Another (12th century A.D.) fixed into a wall records a provision made by Kaṇḍan-uḍaiyār alias Uyyavandān Sāttan of Māṅgāḍu to god Tirumakkāḷam-varam-uḍaiya-Nāyaṇār at [O]lugarai alias Kūḷittūṅga-śōḷanallūr. A third near the well (13th century A.D.) mentions a certain accountant of the nāḍu named Oḷugarai-uḍaiyār.

cells.place: Slab lying in front of the temple of Kāleśvara †
cells.date: Śaka 1393, Vikriti, Arpasi 13, tṛitīyāśī, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 262: Sāḷuva Narasiṅgadēva-Mahārāya. Śaka 1393, Vikriti, Arpaśi 13, trayōdaśi, Monday. Irregular. See also Nos. 111 and 213 of 1934-35.]
cells.remarks: States that, as the temples and several villages in the sīmai of the temple of Tiruppulippagava-Nāyaṇār had been deserted and fallen into ruin for several years owing to the Oḍḍiyan-gaḷahām, Amaramas, the agent of the king, undertook the work of restoring them. He also made a gift by the master, to the restoration of the mānya grants enjoyed by the temples previously.

the Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti took place on Tuesday, 24th December.]

cells.place: Pillar in the mukha-maṇḍapa of Chēnnakēśava temple. †
cells.remarks: States that as the four-pillared manḍapa was found insuffi- cient to accommodate the deity on the day of the festival, Śankaranas, son of Aizzaram Mallanayaka built the six-pillared manḍapa and provided for offerings to the god as the gift of Achyutadēva-Mahārāya. cells.place: South and west walls of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Records gift of money by a certain Veḷān Gaṇavati of Vāttalai Kūḍal for a twilight lamp in the temple in expiation of the sin of having killed Achchan Sūri, the headman of Kiḷanallūr. This money was utilised for reclaiming land belonging to the temple. It is dated in the 18th year of Perumāl-Udaiyār. On the same wall is found a portion of the historical introduction of Rājarāja II beginning with the words Pū-maruviya.

cells.place: East wall of the prākāra of Kanakāmbikā (outside), north of entrance. †
cells.remarks: Registers a grant of the dispute regarding certain shares of gift-lands granted in the previous year Sōbbakarit and the redistribution of the vritis of the sarvamānya-agrahāra village Śrībhāshyapuram between the Chēnnakēśava temple and the temple managed by Narasingadēva-Mahārāja, son of Nandyāla Narasingadēva-Mahārāja, at the request of the parties. The agrahāra Śrībhāshyapuram comprised the villages Sambabūru and Gaṅdamapalle situated in Amparru-sīma in the Nandyāla-sthala included in the Ghaṇḍikōṭa-sīma belonging to the Udayagiri-chāvadi, which had been granted to Nārāyadēva-Mahārāja as nāyaṁkara by the king.

cells.place: Two slabs set up in the same place
cells.date: Śāka 1575 (wrong), Plavaṅga, Āshāḍha, śu 10, Tuesday, Śrāvaṇa, Abhijit.
cells.remarks: States that the god commanded Nithappa and Gaṅgamma of Chuppalli that, having hitherto been propitiated under the name Chēnnakēśava, (He the god) wished to be wor- shipped thereafter under the name Lakshmi-Nārāyaṇasvāmin, and that according to (the letters) found on the slab, he had assembled the āchāryapurushas and Brahmans and re-named the god as Lakshmi-Nārāyaṇasvāmin. Adds that the money collected from the devotees and the pilgrims should go half for the administration of the village and the other half to the temple, of which the Rāmānujakūṭa and other charities should be maintained.

cells.remarks: Records that Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Satyarasa constructed a temple at Eḍeyanatha and consecrated therein, the god Bikkēśvara named after his father Bikke-arasu and granted lands and fixed taxes on oil-mills for offerings and sa-satra for the ascetics. cells.place: Same pillar
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of 55 sheep made by Mara-Bōyundu, son of Nanne-Bōyu, of Gommavali, for his own merit and for the spiritual welfare of Buddhhavarma, son of the former's nephew Pōnti- Nāyundu, to the temple of Sagarāśvara-Mahādēva, for the merit of their parents. Buddhhavarma who is called 'the guardian of Kuñchīpura', bears some of the epithets of the Kōṇapaṇ[ṭi] chiefs and is stated to have belonged to the Valarāja-kula.

cells.remarks: Stones misplaced and some lost. Registers gift of house-sites, etc., by a Brahman of Tuvūr, for offerings and lamps to the shrine of Tiruchchuśaināchchiyār, a goddess consecrated by Tirumala-dayalliyamman at Kuñjaram alias Tirumalaiyampuram, a hamlet of Iravāṇarāyan in Paranur-kūṟram, a subdivision of Mīlāḍu alias Jananātha-vaḷanāḍu. In characters of the 16th century A.D. Records that, as the maṇyādis of Kuñjaram had emigrated owing to official oppression, they were called back and settled in Kōnēriy-appaṇpēṭṭai with some tax concessions.

cells.date:
Chalukya-Vikrama year 34, Viśvākhin, Mārgasiṛsha puṇ­ṇame, Monday, lunar eclipse, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅ­krānti. [date-calculation appendix, No. 1: Śaka 1461, Viḷambi, Pushya, ba. 30, Sunday
= A. D. 1539, January 19, Sunday : ba. 14 was current till ·17 of th
day and amāvāsyā commenced thereafter.]
cells.remarks: Records a remission of grāmas (taxes) on the land of the temple of Svayambhudēva at Khēda in the One Thousand-division, made by Lakshmidhara-Bhaṭṭōpādhyāya, pre­ceptor of the king's eldest son Yuvarāja Mallikārjunadēva, in favour of the same temple, whereas the latter was governing the Taḍḍavādi-1000 division. Also records gifts of money, income, taxes, etc., made for the same temple by Mahā­pradhāna Permmāḍiyarasa and his subordinate Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Gōvarasa of the Siḷāra family and by the Five Hundred Svāmis of Ayyavoḷe and the Eight nāḍus.

cells.remarks: States that Māyidēva-Daṇḍanāyaka planted trees and inaugurated the charity fair (dharma-srathe) at Bēvūr in Taddavāḍi-1000, in the presence of the gāvuṇḍas, mahājanas and merchants of the place, guilds of the 36-villages division, at the request of Sridēvi, wife of his officer Bōppaṇa-chamūpa, the governor of the 36-villages division. Also records a gift of land and assignment of income by him to the temple of Taddavāḍi-1000 and to Bōppaṇa-Nāyaka, for maintaining the above charities. Minor gifts of trees to the temples of Rēvaṇēśvara, Bhōgēśvara, Taleyakāvēdēva, etc., are also registered.

cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village Vilasī in Kōmāvani-maṇḍala by the king to the scholar Sōmayāji-naman of the Bharadvāja-gōtra who in turn along with his brother Gaṇapaya settled it as an agrahāra in shares to 108 Brahmans well versed in the Vēdas and Sāstras and le assembled in the several places and settled in this village. Relates the circumstances in which the chief rose to power in the Telugu country after the capture and fall of the Kākatiya-Pratāparudra at the hands of the Turushkas (Mussalmans).

cells.place: Tallari of Gundala, Gooty taluk, through the District Collector, Anantapur.
cells.remarks: This plate evidently formed part of a complete document of which the other plates are missing. Seems to record that on receipt of the pirvānā (firman) of the Nawnb demanding compensation for the maintenance of those com- mitted within the limits of some lands at Prākat tachacheruvu, the residents of the village represented that the lands were not liable to payment of tax because Peda Timma and Chinna Timma living at Nakkadoddi village and that accordingly the latter who were approached by the messengers agreed to give no com- pensation after satisfying themselves that the lands were really theirs. The characters seem to belong to the 17th century A.D.

cells.remarks: The inscription is engraved in characters assignable to the about 12th century A.D. The language is an obscure mixture of Kannada and Sanskrit. Mentions king receives a number of Western Chālukya birudas. Seems to record a grant of land and house-site in the village Maramuri made by the king, while camping, in the course of his Kapadi-Saṅgāma campaign in the south, to a victorious campaign in the south, to a certain Rāmānāyāṇḍa. (Cf. C.P. No. 1 of 1935-36).

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Ēragapalle-(Hamlet of Ambhavaram). Slab set up in front of the Narasimha temple.
cells.date: Śaka 1470, Plavaṅga, Kārttika, śu. 15, lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Registers grant of land made by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Chenna-kēśavarāja, son of Aparañji and grandson of Apratikamalla Bōdhayanam-Rāmarāja of the Āravīṭi-vaṁśa and belonged to the Kāśyapa-gōtra, Āpastamba-sūtra and the Sāma-vaṁśa, for daily offerings to god Narasimha of the village Bommavaram situated in the hōra-grāma Ambavaram in Oḍḍavādi-sīma. The slab is said to have been granted by the king Acyutarāya to Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Rāmarāja China-Timmayyadēva-Mahārāja and the latter chief granted the hōra-grāma Ambavaram as umbaḷi to the donor. At the top are carved the Vaḍagalai Vaishṇava mark along with śaṅkha and Chakra.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT · Mōyilakalava — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Slab lying in front of the Veṅkaṭēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Registers grant of land and certain taxes (śīla-sunka) made by Rāyasam Veṅgaḷappayya, son of Udayagiri Vīraṇa-yya, in favour of the temple of Veṅkaṭēśvara-svāmi at Mōyilakalava consecrated by him at Mōyilakalava in Kāḷahasti-sīma, for the merit and worship for the merit of his guru Tāḷḷapākkam Tirumalayyaṅgāru. Also registers the grant of the dommaripannas made by him. A further gift of land by the mahājanas of Rāmpāṭāḍu to the god is also recorded. Also provides various kinds of fruit trees planted by the donor (Vīraṇayya). A further grant of the grāmakatnam and aḍu vaḷḷu taxes of the village Mōyilakalava is made by a certain Chiṭṭalūri Yellayya for the merit of Vīraṇayya.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT · NELLORE DISTRICT. / KANIGIRI TALUK. — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Nallajanampādu.—(Hamlet of Rājupālem.) Slab living in a field 2 miles north east of the village.
cells.remarks: In characters of the 9th century A.D. Registers a gift of land sowbhāga with three pillars of the temple to Bhaṭṭi-Pinnama, son of Bhaṭṭi-Rāya, who bears the titles Paramā-sāmi, Mahēsvara, Paramēśvara and Pallavāditya and is said to be a worshipper at the feet of Bhagavad-Ahiñta Paramā-bhāga-raka. Published in Nellore Inscriptions, Vol. II, pp. 670-77.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT — Tamil Nadu
NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT · GUNTUR DISTRICT. / PALNAD TALUK. — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Mācherla.—A hero-stone near the Chandravānka river.
cells.remarks: Impression received from Mr. Seshadri Sastri, P.A., I.T., of Guntur. States that Āsa[k]uṇjubhū entered the army of Birudu Gāmaya, son of Uriya-Bētarája and Mahādevi-Mēgama and offered his head to Paḍjāsani (goddess), for his master. The sculpture of the hero was made by Vaṇikō-juṇḍu Iruga, i.e., Iruga, son of Vaṇikōja.

cells.date: Śaka 954, Pārthiva, Pushya, śu. 12, Monday, Uttarāyaṇa-saṁkrānti. [date-calculation appendix, No. 110: Bhuvanaikamalla (Sōmēśvara II). Śaka 994, Paridhāvin, Pushya, śu. 12, Monday, Uttarāyana-saṅkrānti =A. D. 1072, December 24, Monday ; f.d.t. ·11.]
cells.remarks: Informs that Kaichala-Mahādēvi was carrying on the Government from the headquarters at Muluguṇḍa, with Mahāpradhāna Daṇḍanāyaka Rudrabhaṭṭōpādhyāya administrating the province under Gudigere. Rudrabhaṭṭa's son Bhaṭṭa in charge of all the departments. Records the revival of the endowment of the Cudigere-grāma with the consent of Rudrabhaṭṭōpādhyāya in favour of Nandi-guṇḍa-grāma and some other localities. The charities mentioned above on the occasion of the victorious return of Rudrabhaṭṭōpādhyāya from the northern expedition.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT · HANGAL TALUK. — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Ādir.—Stone standing on the top of a hill (Survey No. 146).
cells.remarks: The characters belong to the seventh century A. D. Registers a gift of a field for the dānasāla of a Jinalaya constructed by a gāmuṇḍa. Records again the grant of a paddy-field to the west of Karmagālūr, for the benefit of the same temple of Jinēśvara, by Dōṇa gāmuṇḍa and others with the permission of the mahāmantrika Aṇṇayyarasa who was ruling the world and Sindharasa was governing the city of Pāṇḍivūra. (Published in Ind. Ant. Vol. XI, p. 69 ff.).
